post.author: BobLoukas
post.text:
The transition from a bear to bull phase can be tricky to position for, especially when you don't get capitulation deep into a Cycles timing band.

This is the case for Bitcoin currently. There are clear signs of a bottom with some confirming elements, but not definitive confirmation of a bottom yet. And even with a price low in place, the likelihood of chop or a retest of the lower regions is real. Investors who rode out the bear can still give a lot back as a market transitions.

Based on what I'm seeing here, if I had a gun to head, I would say the price lows are in for Bitcoin. But it probably won't be as easy as that, meaning the market will likely need to shake out some of this early exuberance we're seeing on the feed.

I'll record the next 4yr Cycle video later this week to discuss how I'm thinking about deploying the last tranche.

post.author: BobLoukas
post.text:
To my long time silver friends, why Silver is more likely heading to $46 before turning bullish again.  

Silver blow-off moves take a lot of time to retrace and rebuild a base.  And often the last weekly cycle from the blowoff phase has to be retraced, in this case to $46.  

From a trend perspective, this remains an intermediate time frame retracement from the January blow-off move. The arrows show the corresponding gold Cycle highs/low, which are in decline.  And the next weekly cycle low is not due until the end of 2026.

From past experience, Silver in a bull market offers one of the best opportunities to post significant portfolio gains. It's because when it goes into a parabolic advance, it's generally just one relentless and straight move up, allowing for good positions to sit tight in. But those parabolic moves are short-lived (6 to 12 months) and then it takes a long time for another such environment to build.  

I feel strongly that Silver will go through another such environment in the near future, but know that it's always a process.
